transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-31 16:00 UTC | Duration 52m | Attendees listed in metadata

Summary section (auto): quick walkthrough of Console rate policies, API behaviors, and Optimize suggestions; covered dedicated capacity considerations and security ask list.

00:00 Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, mike, sara, jordan. we are going to run through how Redwood handles tenant governance and adaptive backpressure, mainly via org keys and project keys, and show the console and API flows.
00:22 Mike (CTO): Great, thanks, alex. to frame it, quantum data runs streaming enrichment and long-tail batch jobs. our peak is about 4k rps for short bursts, sustained ~600 rps. priority for us is fairness between customers and not letting one tenant saturate our cost budget.
00:38 Priya (SE): Yep, understood. we'll demo a couple of patterns: org-level quotas that cap global spend, project-level keys for per-app isolation, and an adaptive backpressure policy that reduces concurrency and falls back to a cheaper model when limits hit.
00:55 Sara (Platform Eng): Quick Q — are org keys and project keys both JWT-based? how do you rotate them?
01:04 Priya (SE): Good question, the API keys are scoped; org key is top-level and can mint project keys. rotation can be automated via KMS/HSM integrations or manual rotate in the console. there's a short-lived key option that we demo in the console.
01:22 Jordan (Data Eng): do you have sticky routing? we want to keep cached KV shards warm for some tenants.
01:30 Jon (SE): Yeah, we have sticky routing options per policy so a tenant can be pinned to a pool. that keeps kv cache hot; we also showed affinity in previous benchmarks but we'll show it here in the console -> routing rules.
01:46 Anita (Security): are audit logs immutable? we need them for compliance audits and need an export path to our S3.
01:54 Priya (SE): All audit trails can be exported; we support S3 sinks and partner KMS for envelope encryption. logs are append-only in the control plane and the customer can configure retention.
02:08 Alex (AE): Okay turning over to Priya for the Console demo — she'll pop open the policy editor and show a sample org quota.
02:15 Priya (SE): (screen share) Alright, console home, route to Organizations > Quantum Data > Rate Policies. This sample policy caps at 10m tokens/day at org-level and then per-project burst windows. you'll see an adaptive backpressure pane here, which has thresholds for queue length and p95 latency.
02:40 Priya (SE): If we simulate a spike, the policy engine will first apply fairshare then throttle by concurrency, then reduce the target model to a quantized variant for best-effort. note, the reduce-model step is pluggable — you choose variants per route.
03:05 Jordan (Data Eng): when you say reduce-model do you mean fallback to a different model family or quantized variant?
03:12 Priya (SE): Both. you can either map to a smaller architecture or a 4-bit quantized variant in the same family. the console shows expected token cost delta so you can tune thresholds to hit cost SLOs.
03:30 Mike (CTO): latency is a big deal — can we guarantee p95 under 300ms for 1k concurrent requests?
03:40 Jon (SE): Our Dedicated tier gives predictable throughput; for that p95 you'd want reserved pools sized to your 1k concurrency target. we can show historical perf curves; for hosted there's soft SLOs and autoscale.
03:52 Priya (SE): Also note we have a 'graceful degradation' chain — reduce concurrency, then batch more aggressively, then fallback model, then return 429 as last resort. you can reorder those steps per route.
04:12 Sara (Platform Eng): Is batching safe for your telemetry pipelines? if you batch too much it affects per-message latencies.
04:21 Priya (SE): The runtime is sequence-length aware; batching is workload-aware so small messages don't get held long. there's also a latency budget per route so you can keep p50/p95 targets.
04:35 Alex (AE): we'll pause the demo for a sec — mike, curious on timeline, if pilot goes well are you thinking hosted pilot or do you need dedicated from day one?
04:45 Mike (CTO): We prefer hosted for quick validation but will probably move to Dedicated for the production tenants with strict SLAs. security team insists on private networking for some customers, so VPC peering or Private deployment will be required.
05:02 Anita (Security): yes, plus we need SSO (SAML), RBAC, and KMS for key material. are those supported in pilot?
05:12 Priya (SE): Yes — pilot can include SAML SSO and KMS integration, though for HSM-backed keys there's an enterprise onboarding step. we'll include integration docs in the security packet.
05:28 Jon (SE): Back to policy flows: here is a rule where org spend limit is enforced as a token budget; if a project would push org over limit it sees a blocking 429 and we surface a soft quota to the calling app with a header x-redwood-remaining. we also support pre-flight quota checks via /quota-status on the API.
05:49 Jordan (Data Eng): that header will help us circuit-break upstream — good. can we get granular metrics per key and per-route?
05:56 Priya (SE): Yes, per-key token counts, latency percentiles, cost breakdown per token and per model, and you can create alerts on model-regression or cost spikes.
06:12 Alex (AE): let's try a simulated spike — Priya will run a 10k rps synthetic for 30s against a project key and we'll watch fairshare and backpressure kick in.
06:22 Priya (SE): (typing) launching synthetic load... 10k rps is simulated but note our console shows queuing rising and concurrency trimming now. you can see one tenant's qps tripped the org soft quota and then the policy demoted model after the concurrency threshold.
06:40 Mike (CTO): i see the events in the timeline but the labels are a little off — the transcript tool sometimes shows speaker 2 for you, priya.
06:48 Alex (AE): yeah fireflies sometimes mislabels; ignore that.
06:52 Sara (Platform Eng): are there built-in backoff headers we can honor? meaning does redwood return Retry-After or x-backoff-suggested?
07:00 Priya (SE): we return standard Retry-After on hard 429s and a structured header x-redwood-backoff with suggested cooldown and a reason code. you can wire that into the client's retry middleware.
07:15 Jordan (Data Eng): okay, for our bench we want to reproduce our 5-minute blast working set and then a 2-hour gradual ramp. what tooling do you recommend?
07:25 Jon (SE): we'll share a traffic-replay harness that supports variable arrival curves and tokenization parity. it's in the SE repo; we'll include a small docker image and a k6 script.
07:35 Mike (CTO): rough numbers: we need p95 < 300ms for priority tenants at 1k concurrency and cost per 1k tokens below $0.35 — is that reasonable?
07:46 Priya (SE): cost targets depend on model choice and batching; Optimize can suggest model/quantization combos. $0.35 per 1k tokens seems high — double-check units? Typically we quote per-token or per-1k tokens on the pricing sheet. we'll send a modeled cost table.
07:58 Anita (Security): anything in the policy editor that logs decisions for compliance? we need to show why a request was throttled.
08:06 Priya (SE): each decision emits an event with policy id, rule matched, and the decision chain; those are stored in audit logs and available via the Events API. customers can retain or export them for audits.
08:20 Alex (AE): switching to API patterns quickly — you'll use org key to do cross-tenant admin tasks and create project keys for each service. here's a curl example.
08:29 Priya (SE): (reads aloud) curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <project-key>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-base","input":"..."}' — the response includes x-redwood-remaining and x-redwood-model used.
08:45 Jordan (Data Eng): do you support scoped keys that limit endpoints (embedding only vs generate)?
08:50 Priya (SE): yes, key scopes are granular to method and route. we often recommend least-privilege for ingestion workers.
09:00 Mike (CTO): what about burst credit windows — can we bank unused quota?
09:06 Jon (SE): We support burst windows via token pooling. org-level pool can smooth short bursts and you can configure refill rates; unused tokens can expire or persist per policy.
09:20 Sara (Platform Eng): for sticky routing we want deterministic placement — is that an additional cost?
09:27 Priya (SE): No extra cost for affinity routing, but it may require capacity planning on Dedicated pools to reserve nodes for hot tenants.
09:36 Alex (AE): / Optimize — priya, show the suggestions view.
09:40 Priya (SE): (screen) Optimize runs offline analysis on historical traces and recommends batching size, model variant, and cache TTLs. here it suggests a 1.8x batching multiplier for low-latency routes and quantize some background routes to 4-bit to save ~55% token cost.
10:00 Mike (CTO): can Optimize run on a replayed trace in our environment or only on Redwood-hosted traces?
10:08 Priya (SE): We accept uploaded traces (anonymized) and can run Optimize in a private project for your pilot under NDA. that way recommendations reflect your exact traffic.
10:20 Jordan (Data Eng): good. for the pilot we need to see per-tenant regression monitoring — if quality drops when quantized, we need alerts tied to our evals.
10:30 Priya (SE): We support eval sets and can surface regression alerts per route with configurable thresholds and tie them to a canary rollout.
10:42 Anita (Security): A few checklist items: SOC2, ISO, SAML, KMS, audit export, penetration test results. we'll need them before pilot kickoff.
10:53 Alex (AE): we'll compile a security packet. Priya will include steps for SAML and KMS integration and a contact for the enterprise onboarding team.
11:02 Mike (CTO): billing and quotas: can we have spend caps that automatically block usage? we need hard caps for some cost centers.
11:10 Jon (SE): Yes, hard caps enforced at org-level can block further requests; you get alerts and a soft quota warning when threshold is near. you'll also see a per-project spend forecast in the Console.
11:22 Jordan (Data Eng): do you expose per-request cost in logs? we'd like to correlate against our billing.
11:28 Priya (SE): Per-request cost is included in the event payload; you can export to our billing API or pull the cost table via the Usage API.
11:36 Mike (CTO): ok lets talk about success criteria — for pilot we want: 1) reproduce our 5-minute blast with p95 < 300ms for priority tenants, 2) per-tenant cost within 10% of forecast, 3) audit log export validated. if those pass we'll plan a 3-month dedicated transition for top tier tenants.
11:58 Alex (AE): great, we'll put those as acceptance criteria in the pilot doc and attach it to the contract.
12:05 Priya (SE): closing demo notes — we'll send the bench harness, the security pack, and a sample pilot contract. any final questions?
12:14 Anita (Security): timeline for docs?
12:18 Alex (AE): Priya will send the technical artifacts by Friday (2026-04-02), and I'll send pricing and pilot terms tomorrow (2026-04-01).
12:28 Mike (CTO): sounds good. thanks everyone.
12:34 (call ends)
